mcqs.learning_point: Recognise roles and responsibilities within families
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is a common misconception about roles and responsibilities in a typical Indian family?

options.A: Both parents share earning and household chores.
options.B: Only fathers make all financial decisions for the family.
options.C: Children help with small tasks such as setting the table.
options.D: Grandparents may provide childcare support to their grandchildren.

mcqs.answer: Only fathers make all financial decisions for the family.
mcqs.explanation: Option B is a misconception. In many Indian families, financial decisions are increasingly shared between parents, and sometimes other members contribute as well. Options A, C, and D correctly describe common practices, whereas B reflects an outdated stereotype.

mcqs.question: A family decides to prepare dinner together: one member washes vegetables, another chops them, a third cooks, and the fourth sets the table. Why is this cooperation important for the household?

options.A: It reduces the time each person spends on the task, allowing more leisure time.
options.B: It ensures that only the most skilled member does the work.
options.C: It creates competition among members to see who works faster.
options.D: It makes the meal taste better because more people are involved.

mcqs.answer: It reduces the time each person spends on the task, allowing more leisure time.
mcqs.explanation: Cooperation distributes workload, so tasks are completed faster and with less fatigue, giving family members more time for rest or other activities. Option B is incorrect because cooperation values contribution over skill alone. Option C misrepresents cooperation as competition, and Option D confuses cooperation with culinary quality.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the traditional joint family with the modern nuclear family in India?

options.A: Joint families consist of only parents and their children, while nuclear families include grandparents and extended relatives.
options.B: Joint families involve multiple generations living together, whereas nuclear families typically comprise only parents and their children.
options.C: Both joint and nuclear families always have the same number of members, but differ in income levels.
options.D: Nuclear families are a recent invention that completely replace joint families in all Indian societies.

mcqs.answer: Joint families involve multiple generations living together, whereas nuclear families typically comprise only parents and their children.
mcqs.explanation: Option B accurately reflects the structural difference: joint families have grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins under one roof, while nuclear families are limited to parents and their children. Option A reverses the definitions. Option C is false because family size varies. Option D overstates the replacement; joint families still exist alongside nuclear families.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the importance of care and mutual support
mcqs.question: Why is mutual care and support considered a vital function of the family as a social institution?

options.A: It guarantees that every family member will achieve the same career success.
options.B: It provides emotional security and helps members cope with personal and social challenges.
options.C: It ensures that families can avoid all conflicts and disagreements.
options.D: It allows families to become financially independent of the larger community.

mcqs.answer: It provides emotional security and helps members cope with personal and social challenges.
mcqs.explanation: Mutual care and support give members a safe environment to express feelings, receive encouragement, and face difficulties such as illness, loss, or academic pressure. Option A is unrealistic; families cannot guarantee identical career outcomes. Option C is false because conflicts can still arise. Option D misinterprets the role of families, which are not isolated from the community.
